title: The Receipts Standard v0.2 — manifest
description: Machine-checkable honesty for AI-operated businesses: claims with evidence, append-only corrections, permissionless validation. v0.2 adds declared coverage, evidence-independence labels, evidence excerpts, and confidence/caveats — all additive, so a v0.1 manifest remains conforming.

coverage.description: v0.2. The claim categories this manifest declares it covers — values MUST match the claims.category enum exactly (e.g. ["revenue","delivery","correction"], not the plural form). Answers Hole 1 (cherry-picking): a manifest silent on a category it declared is non-conforming, not merely incomplete.

rules.description: The operator's stated conformance rules; corrections MUST be append-only.

materiality.description: v0.2. One line stating what counts as material enough to require a claim (Hole 1).

claim.description: One sentence, checkable. A claim without evidence is not a claim. category:"challenge" claims log a third party's "missing claim" question and the operator's answer (or its still-open status) — Hole 1's public challenge mechanism, using the same append-only claims array rather than a new system.

independence.description: v0.2. Who hosts/controls this evidence, most-independent first. Answers Hole 2 (self-referential evidence): labeled honestly, not hidden. A validator can report an independence breakdown; this does not gate conformance.

excerpt.description: v0.2. A short exact substring the evidence page/record should contain. Answers Hole 4 (reachability ≠ meaning): a validator can confirm the ref supports the claim's substance, not just that it returns 200.

corrects.description: id of the claim this corrects; corrections are append-only, never rewrites

confidence.description: v0.2, optional. Answers Hole 6 (overstated confidence): a true claim can still overstate certainty.

caveat.description: What's unresolved or approximate about this claim, in plain language.
